summary: BifrOSt has no object graph, managed object context, fetch request or persistent store layer. Apps persist their data as small atomically replaced text or JSON files through Codable, UserDefaults and the document layer, and the undo manager and snapshot diffing cover some of what Core Data's undo and table data sources do. Persistent history, migrations and CloudKit mirroring have no on-device counterpart; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud.

Work can run off the main loop with dispatch, and the app must do its own store locking. There is no fetch-result object with progress notification.
Diffing turns two identifier lists into insert, remove and move edits. Nothing binds the results of a query to a table automatically, and the app must recompute the list.

features.note: Serial queues give the single-writer pattern. Batch insert and batch delete over a store do not exist because the store is a file, not a database.
Coordinated file access prevents torn writes between processes. There are no per-object merge policies.

gaps: No object graph: no entity model, relationships, inverse relationships or delete rules.
No fetch requests or predicates; apps filter in-memory vectors.
No managed object context with change tracking, dirty state or faulting.
No database-backed store, so stores are rewritten whole on each save and do not scale past the bounded lists (contacts MAX_ITEMS 10000, calendar MAX_EVENTS 2048).
No persistent history or transaction log of store changes.
No migration path between store versions (lightweight, staged or manual).
No fetched results controller that binds a query to a table or list.
No on-device CloudKit-style mirroring or sharing; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud.
